 St. Paul man jumps onto moving school bus after driver’s medical emergency, saving 18 kids
 By KSTP 
 --> 
 Man jumps onto moving bus in St. Paul to save kids
 A St. Paul man’s quick action helped save 18 children on a school bus after the driver suffered a medical emergency.
 It happened Monday afternoon after school in Dayton’s Bluff neighborhood.
 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS reviewed store surveillance video that showed Ebro Ahmed outside Bricks Snacks and Tobacco before he saw what was happening and ran onto the still-moving bus.
 “I saw a bus roll past me with the doors open, and I saw the bus driver seizing up,” Ahmed told 5 EYEWITNESS NEWS on Tuesday.
 Ahmed said he focused on stopping the bus, then called for help.
 “So I just ran out to the bus, I tried to put it in park, I threw it in reverse by accident, and then I ended up getting it in neutral, pulled the parking brake,” said Ahmed. “And then I called the police and called the ambulances so they could help the driver.”
 Ahmed said he counted 18 kids on the bus when police arrived. Fortunately, none were hurt, and the driver is also expected to be OK.
 Ahmed said he doesn’t have any medical experience; instead, he gave credit to a TV show called “Grey’s Anatomy.”
 He added that he wasn’t concerned about credit but is happy everyone is OK.
 “At the end of the day, youth are the most innocent humans on Earth, so anything you can do to save them, help them, it’s worth it,” he said, adding, “Saving lives is very, you know, something God will never forget; God will definitely reward you heavily for it.”
 Ahmed said he is grateful this did not happen on the highway or on a busy street because the outcome could have been much worse.
 St. Paul Public Schools said a medical emergency occurred on a bus route from Battle Creek Middle School and that paramedics responded to the scene. 
 In a Wednesday update, the school district said the driver was released from the hospital and is resting at home. 
 The district said another bus picked the students up and continued their route home, and the school’s mental health team checked in with the kids.
